paper_title: Gas-rich dwarf galaxies as a new probe of dark matter interactions with ordinary matter
notes: Paper derives constraints on ultra-light hidden-photon dark matter (HPDM) with kinetic mixing parameter g (labeled chi in Fig. 2) from heating of gas in the Leo T dwarf galaxy, over mass range 10^-23 to 10^-10 eV. Coupling type is clearly DarkPhoton (hidden photon kinetic mixing). Numerical data points are only available in Fig. 2 (log-log plot) and could not be read precisely; the emitted points are rough estimates reflecting the increasing trend of the exclusion with mass (bound on g scales roughly with mass since heating rate ~ m^2 g^2/omega_p^2 for m << omega_p). DM density is set by the Leo T Burkert halo model (astrophysical, spatially varying), so no single haloscope density is quoted. This is a DM-search-like astrophysical bound.
